How sharp the shadows of characters, vehicles and weapons are. Xbox is the original's soft, blocky shadow; each step up is crisper, and costs a little more of the graphics card.
Lights characters and weapons smoothly, without the flat facets of the Xbox's lighting, at a small cost.
Enhanced: plasma bolts, muzzle flashes and blasts light their surroundings smoothly, with a glow. Classic lights them as the Xbox did.|Classic for everyone in a Pro 2v2 game; yours again after it.

World: soft shade where characters, vehicles and scenery meet the level and each other, from the level's shape; the levels keep their own lighting. Ray Traced: the shade of characters and vehicles traced by the graphics card, where it can (else World).
How deep ambient occlusion World's shade is where characters, vehicles and scenery meet the level.

Smooth: the levels' own light without its bands and blocky edges. Relit Pages: the relight pack's pages where the data folder has them (otherwise Smooth); not PRISM Rebaked, which is a Lighting of its own.
Characters, weapons and vehicles catch the level's own lights as highlights, where their armour is shiny. Off draws them as the Xbox did.
Local: shiny armour reflects the place it is in, from probes in the data folder; none come with the game. Without them, as Classic.

Sun: the sky's sun casts real shadows of characters, vehicles and scenery onto the level and each other. Soft and Traced: characters shade themselves from the main light (need ambient occlusion World). Classic keeps the Xbox's shadows alone.
How sharp Sun's shadows are, and how much of the graphics card they take.
How fast Sun's shadows soften away from what casts them. A dim sun or moon softens them more.
Sharp: the sun's shadows in the levels' own baked light drawn crisp, from a sun map baked on this computer from your maps. Each place keeps its brightness. Off draws the lightmaps' own soft edges.
How far Baked Shadows' Sharp goes: Light keeps some of the lightmaps' softness, Deep darkens the shaded side more.

Game Shaders: the baked light takes the game's light's place under its own textures, highlights and reflections. PRISM Materials: every surface lit by PRISM's materials alone (darker where the game's reflections lit it).
How characters, vehicles and weapons are lit. Baked: by the baked light where they are. Never Darker: the baked light, but never darker than Classic lit them.
How sharp the game's own object shadows are, which PRISM Rebaked draws while Ray Tracing's Object Shadows are Classic's.
Quality: a bounce of light traced at every pixel. Performance: the bounced light read from the bake where the level has it, a bounce traced for the characters and vehicles alone; faster.

PRISM: the traced light smoothed over the frames before and the pixels about. DLSS RR: NVIDIA DLSS Ray Reconstruction (offered once installed), which also brings the view to the screen's resolution; from the next start. Off: the light as traced, grainy (for checking).|DLSS: a plugin you build (prism-plugins README).
How bright the picture is made. Default and Eye: adapts as an eye does, a dark place staying darker than a bright one. Classic's: kept as bright as Classic's frame. Fixed: the light as it is.
Brighter or darker than the exposure chooses, in stops: +1 twice as bright, -1 half.
How light past white is drawn. Default and Filmic: rolled off gently, nothing darker moved. ACES: punchier, a film's curve. Local: as Filmic here. Clipped: held at white, as Classic did.

Draws the 3D view smaller and brings it to the screen's resolution, sharp and anti-aliased: faster. FSR 3.1 is built in; DLSS, offered once installed, from the next start.|DLSS: a plugin you build (prism-plugins README).
How much of the screen's resolution the 3D view is drawn at under the upscaler: Quality 67% each way, Balanced 58%, Performance 50%, Ultra Performance 33%; Native all of it, anti-aliased alone.

While Playing: a level's light is baked in the background as you play it, a quick draft first, then finished, picking up where it stopped. When Asked: only after Rebake Lightmaps. Both PRISM lightings read the bake.
Max: the finest light and sharpest shadows, each texel baked until its noise is gone; slow, and large on disk. The others are quicker and smaller.

Sky: the sky lights each place by how much of it the place sees, as in a path tracer: open ground fully, under cover less, a room with no sky only by what comes in. Flat: the game's own fill, the same everywhere. A change bakes again.
Change this to bake the level you are playing again from nothing (needed after its geometry, materials or lights change; a finished bake is otherwise kept).
Shows "Baking lightmaps 37%" at the top left while a level is baked.
